propositions: The sweep's per-ticket authorship ledger calculation performs one full-history git walk per ticket inside the store write lock, O(N tickets * history depth), causing stalls of 24+ minutes on large stores; hoisting the walk out-of-lock and batching into one store-wide map via build_introducing_commit_map reduces this to O(history depth + events).

The sweep re-yields to concurrent writers only once before the fold loop, so a writer arriving mid-sweep must wait for all remaining tickets; re-probing write_lock_is_busy between chunks ensures fair yielding.
Scoped staging in _commit_backfill via git add <ticket> prevents a concurrent writer's in-flight events from being committed under the compactor's message.
The operation-linked trigger correctly avoids re-triggering while a sweep is running, using a stamped advisory lock inherited from the drain's lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale pattern.
Two mechanisms converge: scheduled 6-hourly sweep where CI exists, and operation-linked fallback triggered from close after lock release for stores with no CI and no cron.
